clue.text: Witch whom the cat eventually crosses

indicators.note: the answer spans across the run of words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A black cat finally crosses the path of a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses' signals that the answer runs across the words 'the cat eventually', starting at the H of 'the'; 'whom' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, the queen of the witches in Macbeth.

clue.text: Weapon breaks armistice shortly

indicators.note: breaks suggests the letters are broken up and rearranged
shortly tells us to cut the word short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A sword shatters a ceasefire before it has had time to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims ARMISTICE to ARMISTIC, and 'breaks' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Brief portent: go about a mile in the lead

indicators.note: in the lead puts the mile's letter at the front of everything else

parts.note: a portent is an omen

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A runner sees a bad omen while briefly leading by a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' looks like a verb of motion but is a noun, a try; 'about' wraps it round A and 'in the lead' sets the mile first.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentary means lasting only a moment, so brief is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rumour one's overcome by bouquet

indicators.note: overcome by means covered over, so the bouquet word wraps round the one

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose, its smell
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Gossip says someone was overpowered by the scent of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks floral, but in wine-tasting it is the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise in the older sense is talk or report, as in a story being noised abroad, a rumour.

clue.text: Wretched in a ragged garment

indicators.note: ragged suggests the letters are torn about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserable figure dressed in a tattered coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' rearranges the eleven letters of 'Wretched in a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A windcheater is a windproof jacket, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Equip a soldier

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marine, a British soldier

explanation.surface: An order to kit out a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: RM is the Royal Marines, the British navy's soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm someone is to equip them with weapons, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spanish girl given a whistle, perhaps, improves a bit

parts.note: a referee is someone given a whistle, abbreviated REF
Ines is a Spanish girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl handed a whistle gets a little better at playing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a whistle, perhaps' describes the person handed a whistle at a match, the referee, shortened as usual; the Spanish girl's name follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine something is to polish it, making small improvements.

clue.text: Beer taken round a camp

indicators.note: taken round means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Drinks are carried round a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: A laager is the Afrikaans name for a defensive camp inside a ring of wagons.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is an encampment protected by a circle of wagons.

clue.text: Surrealist secures right Republican paper

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the painter's name grips the letters inside

parts.note: Joan Miro was a Spanish surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A surrealist artist gets a right-wing newspaper on board.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mirror is a well-known British daily newspaper.

clue.text: Time to go on at length? Not here

definitions.text: Time to go on at length? Not here

parts.note: to witter is British slang for chattering on at length

explanation.surface: If you want to ramble on, this is not the place for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it: Twitter limited posts to 140 characters, so going on at length was not possible there.
explanation.definitionFit: The social network's short character limit made long rambling impossible on it.

clue.text: Bible seen by a woman

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A woman is seen carrying a Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible; 'seen by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava is a woman's first name, as with the actress Ava Gardner.

clue.text: Hurtful to take advantage, but very modern

parts.note: a cutting remark is a hurtful one
to have the edge is to have an advantage

explanation.surface: Being nasty to get ahead is the latest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting-edge technology is the most advanced, at the forefront of development.

clue.text: Sauce quickly runs out

indicators.note: out means the letter is taken away

parts.note: presto is a musical direction meaning quickly
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: The sauce supply is rapidly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R (runs, in cricket scoring) from PRESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Club, as it happens, run with leisure facility

parts.note: a live broadcast is shown as it happens
a swimming pool is a leisure facility

explanation.surface: A club whose events are broadcast in real time, with a swimming pool on site.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool FC is a famous English football club.

clue.text: Be dazed as actresses dancing without clothes initially

indicators.note: dancing suggests letters moving about into a new order
without means the following letter is taken out
initially picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Seeing actresses dancing naked would leave anyone stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes initially' gives C; 'without' removes it from ACTRESSES, leaving ATRESSES, which 'dancing' rearranges. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To see stars is an idiom for being dazed, as after a blow to the head.

clue.text: Not entirely properly stopping television finally before midnight

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the shortened word fills the middle of the other
not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: doing something well is doing it properly

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Switching the TV off just before midnight is not quite the right thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' clips the last letter, 'stopping' plugs the result into the screen abbreviation, and 'finally' takes the last letter of 'before'.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night.

clue.text: Returning here, maybe, treasure receiving cry from cat

indicators.note: receiving means one word takes in the other

parts.note: a hoard is a stash of treasure
a mew is a cat's cry

explanation.surface: Coming back to a treasure trove and hearing a cat miaow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here, maybe' stands for home, so 'returning here' means heading back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeward means going towards home, and home is one place you might call here.

clue.text: Culinary flavouring is combined with essence of mint

parts.note: cum is Latin for with, used for combined with, as in kitchen-cum-diner

indicators.note: essence of means the core, the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe spice blended with a hint of mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'essence of' takes the middle letters of 'mint'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is a spice used to flavour food, especially curries.

clue.text: Container, very small? Bottomless

indicators.note: bottomless means the last letter, the bottom in a down entry, is removed

parts.note: tiny means very small

explanation.surface: Is that container tiny? It has no base.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin is a metal can for storing food.

clue.text: Old set, glass

definitions.meaning: an early type of radio receiver

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an early radio set and fine cut glass.

clue.text: Dislike books, gaining knowledge intuitively

parts.note: to mind something is to dislike or object to it
reading matter is books

explanation.surface: Someone who hates books but picks things up by instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dislike' suggests the reader avoids books; it is simply MIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind-reading is knowing someone's thoughts without being told, by intuition.

clue.text: Confine competitor under canvas with several bonds, potentially

indicators.note: confine means shut inside, so the canvas word encloses the competitor

parts.note: under canvas means camping, in a tent
a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: Lock up the opposition under canvas, with plenty of ties to hold them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confine' shuts the competitor inside the camping shelter; the definition is a chemist's word, three being several.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a trivalent atom can form three bonds, so it could have several.

clue.text: City boundaries keeping man within

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one word contains the other

parts.note: rims are edges or boundaries
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: City walls keep the citizens inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' simply confirms the placement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims, or Reims, is a city in the Champagne region of France.

clue.text: Is concerned by second stroke

parts.note: to care is to be concerned

explanation.surface: Someone worried at being hit a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle stroke or touch.

clue.text: Cooking coconut tart? Get someone else to

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters are mixed up like ingredients

explanation.surface: Baking a coconut tart? Hire someone to do it for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' rearranges the letters of 'coconut tart'.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract out a job is to hand it to another firm under contract.

clue.text: Remarkably fierce animal put in the stew

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the other piece
remarkably suggests the letters are changed into an unusual order

parts.note: an ass is an animal, a donkey

explanation.surface: A ferocious beast is thrown into the cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' rearranges the six letters of 'fierce' to FRICEE, and 'put in' places the donkey inside; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a dish of meat stewed in a thick white sauce.

clue.text: Party faithful certain at heart to regret waste

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letter of the word

parts.note: to rue is to regret
to blue money is old British slang for squandering it

explanation.surface: A loyal member, sure deep down, regrets the party's wastefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes T, the middle letter of 'certain'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: True-blue means staunchly loyal, especially to the British Conservative Party.

clue.text: Clapped-out vehicle — possibly terrier's left inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other word

parts.note: a terrier is an example of a ratter, a dog that catches rats; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: An old banger; perhaps the terrier has been left in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks the terrier as one example of a ratter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattler is slang for a rickety old vehicle that rattles as it goes.

clue.text: Take article that is very concealed

indicators.note: concealed means hidden inside, so the article holds the other letters

parts.note: the is the definite article
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Grab the item, that is, keep it well hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' tucks the Latin abbreviation and V inside the article, between its H and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To thieve is to steal, to take what is not yours.

clue.text: Plain girl, daddy's

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name
pa is a word for daddy, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A plain girl belongs to her father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a description of the girl but it is the noun, a grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are vast treeless plains in South America.

clue.text: Amusing Liberal peer does a turn

indicators.note: does a turn means turns round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of the House of Lords performs a funny routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does a turn' sounds like a comedy act but reverses LORD to DROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means wryly amusing.

clue.text: Bleeding as conflict cranks up

indicators.note: cranks up means is turned upward, so in a down entry the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: war is conflict

explanation.surface: Wounds bleed as fighting intensifies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; 'cranks up' sounds like escalation but reverses WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw wound is open and bleeding.
